reason: The 320-byte scratch stride is the most direct alignment/layout test, but its cache benefit is unknown; the earlier 272-byte stride lost in two of three paired runs, so that result does not predict this layout. The tile-store reorder and TB descriptor paths have specific, checkable changes, with no measured benefit. `assembly_audit` and `n512_fast_path` propose the same TB mapping and conversion, so they should be treated as duplicates if one is selected. Packing B for TB adds a full timed conversion. The A-transpose proposals also add timed conversion work; TT adds two conversions. Transpose fusion lacks a supplied legal instruction recipe, so it ranks low until one is established. The remaining proposals lack an experiment description in the supplied board, so their expected benefit and risk cannot be assessed from this evidence.
